finding: fp16 reduced peak allocated memory by around 47% for both distilgpt2 and gpt2.
evidence: distilgpt2 reduced from 343.41 MB to 181.25 MB; gpt2 reduced from 504.11 MB to 264.78 MB.
why_it_matters: Precision is a major memory optimization lever for LLM inference workloads.

finding: The fp16 reduction was consistent across model sizes.
evidence: distilgpt2 reduction was 47.22%, while gpt2 reduction was 47.48%.
why_it_matters: This suggests that dtype-aware memory estimation can generalize across GPT-style models.

finding: fp16 does not always give exactly 50% total memory reduction.
evidence: Observed reductions were around 47%, not exactly 50%.
why_it_matters: Non-parameter memory, activations, allocator behavior, and framework overhead prevent exact halving.

finding: Precision-aware estimation is required before quantization estimation.
evidence: fp32 and fp16 memory behavior differs significantly.
why_it_matters: This prepares the project for int8/int4 quantization-memory simulation.
